message.text:
h07.

Route: `GET /file/users/:identifier/avatar`. The URL the browser uses is minted server-side — `convertUserToProto` rewrites a base64 avatar into `/file/{user.Name}/avatar` instead of inlining the data (`server/router/api/v1/user_service_converters.go:36`).

Hops from request to stored bytes:

`FileServerService.RegisterRoutes` (route binding) — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:124`
`FileServerService.serveUserAvatar` (handler) — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:168`
`FileServerService.getCurrentUser` (auth gate, only when `!Profile.AllowAnonymous()`) — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:174`
`FileServerService.getUserByUsername` — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:715`
`Store.GetUser` (cache check is ID-only, so this misses) — `store/user.go:148`
`Store.ListUsers` (populates `userCache` per row) — `store/user.go:136`
`store.Driver.ListUsers` (interface boundary) — `store/driver.go:47`
`(*DB).ListUsers` (SQL build + `QueryContext`, selects `avatar_url`) — `store/db/sqlite/user.go:88` (query at `:151`, execution at `:173`)
`FileServerService.parseDataURI` (decode `data:` URI from `user.AvatarURL`) — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:737`
`c.Blob` (response after MIME allowlist + security/cache headers) — `server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:209`

Two things worth noting on this path. The avatar is not a file on disk or in object storage: it's stored inline as a base64 `data:` URI in the `user.avatar_url` column, which is why the last hop is a regex parse rather than a blob fetch. And the response is gated twice — `getUserByUsername` is looked up by username, then the decoded MIME type must be in `avatarAllowedTypes` (`server/router/fileserver/fileserver.go:75`) or the request is rejected with 400. The driver hop shown is SQLite; `store/db/postgres/user.go` and `store/db/mysql/user.go` implement the same interface method for the other dialects. The route is registered during startup at `server/server.go:81`–`82`, ahead of the gRPC gateway.
